name: Kody Technolab Limited
summary: Kody Technolab is a software-services company financing a transition into goods, proprietary robotics, retained advertising robots and connected manufacturing/distribution ventures. This is a speculative product-transition thesis, not an established software compounder. Actual revenue, capitalized technology assets and venue deployments exist; neither TAM nor robot announcements should be dismissed as nothing. The decisive weakness is the missing bridge from those assets and deployments to collected, parent-attributable incremental returns. FY26 consolidated revenue rose 11.86% to ₹80.2818 crore but reported PAT fell 4.88%; normalized operating EBIT fell 10.25%. New unbilled revenue exceeds the total revenue addition. The 19 October close ₹1,556.15 implies ₹2,265.22 crore equity value on current issued shares. That price demands exceptional execution before allowing for dilution and financing. All ordinary return and entry-price outputs are withheld. Hold — unresolved: reconcile financial reliability and current funding, then reassess price. The conclusion could improve with demonstrated collected robot/media economics and independently reconcileable capital allocation; it is not a declaration of fraud or insolvency.

factor_audit.rationale: Disclosures identify RPTs, dilution and failed JV; no substantiated diversion or material default found. Large connected advances, subsidiary fund-raising attribution and unresolved audit annexures prevent above-average stewardship credit. Unmodified IFC is positive counterevidence, not blanket clearance.
factor_audit.missing_evidence: Audit committee reconciliations, bank returns and related-party recoverability.
factor_audit.upgrade_trigger: Reconcile all differences and demonstrate disciplined related-party collections.
factor_audit.downgrade_trigger: Proven misapplication, unapproved related transfers or materially misleading financial reporting.
material_facts: FY26 main and IFC opinions are unmodified.
Falcon loan 24.031 cr and World EMS investment 37.5 cr are disclosed connected exposures.
factor_audit.counterevidence: No substantiated diversion or discriminatory minority transaction established; Vira termination was disclosed.

factor_audit.rationale: Software execution and real retained-fleet deployments are positive, but IP applications, design registrations and launch breadth do not show exclusive economics, pricing power, recurring retention or switching costs. Large global robot peers are not direct sales comparables.
factor_audit.missing_evidence: Patent claims/grants, competitive win-loss, customer retention, gross margins and robot uptime/economic cohorts.
factor_audit.upgrade_trigger: Repeat paid adoption with defensible margins and independent IP/customer evidence.
factor_audit.downgrade_trigger: Deployment does not convert into revenue or competitors commoditize pricing.
material_facts: Management reports 62 LuLu robots at 30 stores.
Patent applications/publication and capitalized development exist, but granted exclusion and unit returns were not verified.
factor_audit.counterevidence: Actual software revenue and venue access show capabilities beyond a paper product; they may mature into switching costs.

factor_audit.starting_rubric: Reported and conservative billed-service proxy both exceed 30%: start 9, Medium-confidence ceiling 8, no further adjustment.
factor_audit.rationale: Predetermined five-year reported CAGR 100.44% starts at 2.4815 cr and crosses a greenfield-group and product transition, not a demonstrated acquisition-led expansion. Three-year reported CAGR 94.25% corroborates substantial growth. Excluding all FY26 goods and unbilled leaves billed services 40.8149 cr; even this conservative proxy exceeds 30% CAGR versus full FY21/FY23 revenue. This is not a precise organic series, but threshold robustness supports starting 9 capped 8 for Medium confidence, with no further small-base or trajectory penalty.
factor_audit.missing_evidence: Comparable organic volumes, billed-to-unbilled/collections bridge, related-party eliminations and demand basis.
factor_audit.upgrade_trigger: Produce comparable organic five-year or justified three-year series with collected contracts.
factor_audit.downgrade_trigger: Unbilled reversals, channel stuffing or material revenue restatement.
material_facts: FY21–FY26 reported revenue increases 2.4815 to 80.2818 cr; five-year CAGR 100.44%.
FY26 billed services 40.8149 cr excluding all goods and unbilled still exceed 30% three/five-year growth versus earlier total sales.
factor_audit.counterevidence: FY26 growth slows 11.86%, goods decline 18.5% and unbilled 10.5406 cr exceeds total revenue addition; exact organic recognition and RPT units need reconciliation.

factor_audit.rationale: Hospital, retail and airport use cases create access to growth. Yet exclusivity and venue presence differ from committed profitable offtake; ad fill and recurring fees unknown. India/MiddleEast footprint offers opportunity without a proven long-duration franchise.
factor_audit.missing_evidence: Contract unit/value floors, customer budgets, advertising utilization, renewals and capital per incremental revenue.

Retained LuLu advertising network claim covers 30 stores and 62 units.
factor_audit.counterevidence: Contract minima values, ad fill and approval-dependent medical monetization are not disclosed; Vira partnership was cancelled.

factor_audit.rationale: FY26 deployed capital grows sharply while normalized operating EBIT falls. Group ROCE is not a valid substitute for attributable incremental returns amid new software assets, JV advances, subsidiaries, outside equity and unresolved NCI. No mature cohort bridge.
factor_audit.missing_evidence: Parent-attributable investment/cash-return cohort; true development capitalization and amortization lives.

sections.title: Executive Summary
sections.text: Kody Technolab is a software-services company financing a transition into goods, proprietary robotics, retained advertising robots and connected manufacturing/distribution ventures. sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Legal identity is Kody Technolab Limited, NSE Emerge SME symbol KODYTECH, ISIN INE0Q7P01013, observed ST series. Information cutoff 20 October 2026, quote 19 October 2026; no post-cutoff operating claims used. No September 2026 half-year results were found in the exchange announcement record by the cutoff; no post-cutoff release is used. Latest available annual financial basis is FY26 consolidated Indian GAAP/Accounting Standards, not IndAS. FY21–FY24 standalone history is displayed separately from FY25–FY26 consolidated. Entry 20 October 2026 and terminal 20 October 2031 give five calendar years with actual-day fiscal interpolation. Hurdle 15% nominal INR, pretax, no dividends assumed. ₹5 lakh is an illustrative execution reference, not personalized allocation. Three 100-share lots cost ₹466,845 and four cost ₹622,460. Primary-source financial numbers are high-confidence transcriptions; comparable organic growth, attribution, normalized returns and current funding have lower confidence. G1 and G4 are Conditional; G2 and G3 Hold — unresolved. Statutory unmodified opinions do not override contradictory annexures. Missing current balance information is evaluated against dated financing and obligations, not an arbitrary demand for daily bank statements.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: BQS, Growth Quality Score and IAS are NS, not zero and not midpoint scores. GOV 5, MOAT 4, REV 8, DUR 5, CASH 4, EXEC 5 and EARN 4 have Medium-confidence evidence. L 7 is supported by 60 official sessions and explicit restrictions. CAP and BAL remain NS because their economic denominators/bases are materially unresolved; R,D and P remain NS rather than translating an unfinanceable diagnostic into an investment recommendation. Exact Decimal contributions and original missing weights are embedded below. BQS known contribution 4.06 with 80% coverage gives mathematical bound 4.26–6.06. GQS known 5.20 with 85% coverage gives 5.35–6.70. IAS known 0.70 with 10% coverage gives 1.60–9.70 because its Q input requires final unrounded BQS. These are mathematical missing-data bounds, not confidence intervals. No weights are redistributed and no generic SME penalty is imposed. Moving GOV and MOAT one point each changes BQS known sum by±0.40; moving DUR and EARN changes GQS by±0.35. These uncertainties are smaller than the missing-data range. G2 independently prevents favorable numerical quality ranking.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: The economic model now combines billed software/design work, goods and retained robot assets. FY24 disclosed ₹18.1647 crore domestic/export software revenue and ₹4.2923 crore robot-parts sales. FY26 consolidated goods are ₹28.9263 crore, billed services ₹40.8149 crore and unbilled export services ₹10.5406 crore. These legal accounting buckets do not establish pure recurring software, robot units, maintenance subscriptions or advertising take rates. Goods require sourcing/manufacturing working capital; project services require delivery and collections; the advertising model requires Kody to retain and maintain the fleet before sharing venue advertising proceeds. Management's October LuLu announcement says 62 Odigos robots at 30 stores; it is a venue/network deployment, not 62 recognized sales. Media subsidiary FY26 revenue ₹2.82475 crore and loss ₹0.617462 crore offer an early audited monetization anchor, while MiddleEast had no FY26 revenue. The Medigo arrangement separates Kody manufacturing, related Falcon distribution and Sccore deployment; undisclosed purchase floors and licensing conditions prevent a bankable order-book assumption. Demand concentration, recurring retention and customer-level economics remain ND.

sections.title: Moat and Industry Position
sections.text: Potential advantage lies in combining software, navigation, systems integration and local maintenance with site access. The mechanism must be tested through retained contracts, uptime, lower cost per task and repeat advertising/customer budgets. Patent filing or publication is not a patent grant or proof of exclusion; design registration protects a different claim from navigation/software functionality. No independent granted-patent registry validation or exclusive economic moat is assumed. Management's product portfolio, deployment and pipeline counts show effort and optionality, not installed profitable share. Software competitors can deliver custom projects; mobile robots face industrial automation vendors, integrators and low-cost imported hardware. Ksolves is a software-services cash benchmark, not a robot competitor: FY26 consolidated revenue ₹162.668 crore, PAT ₹34.3308 crore and CFO ₹30.7678 crore. FANUC's FY25 robot salesJPY 329,566 million declined 13.5%, demonstrating cyclicality even at scale. ABB's FY25 group cash generation and automation scale cannot justify Kody's valuation. No common-date peer P/E table is manufactured without verified peer shares/quotes. MOAT 4 reflects nascent differentiation without evidence of durable excess returns.

sections.title: Revenue Growth and Scale
sections.text: The measurement policy prefers five-year comparable organic CAGR; three years is only a fallback for genuinely comparable data, not a better-looking number. Reported FY21 ₹2.4815 crore to FY26 ₹80.2818 crore is 100.44% CAGR; FY23 ₹10.9524 crore to FY26 ₹80.2818 crore is 94.25%. These are reported mixed-product/group diagnostics, not precise organic estimates. Greenfield subsidiaries and changing mix do not automatically invalidate expansion. FY26 revenue addition ₹8.5100 crore follows FY25 ₹49.3148 crore addition across the move to consolidation and goods/services expansion. FY26 goods declined from ₹35.4941 crore to ₹28.9263 crore; billed services rose from ₹36.2777 to ₹40.8149 crore. Newly disclosed unbilled ₹10.5406 crore exceeds the total annual addition. Excluding current unbilled yields ₹69.7412 crore, below prior total, but this alone does not prove fictitious growth: completed work may legitimately precede billing. What is missing is contract acceptance, timing, customer/RPT mix, collection and like-for-like gross/net bridge. Greenfield subsidiaries are not proof of purchased third-party revenue; do not mechanically label all growth acquired. Domestic/export changes suggest mix shift, not necessarily sustained unit acceleration. As a conservative threshold check, FY26 billed services alone ₹40.8149 crore, excluding every goods sale and all unbilled work, still implies more than 30% five-year and three-year growth versus full earlier revenue. This compares a conservative current numerator with historic standalone/group totals, not a comparable cohort or reconstructed organic series, and does not validate each contract; it bounds the scoring threshold sufficiently for REV 8, from starting 9 and Medium-confidence ceiling 8. No extra trajectory or small-base deduction is imposed. G2 Hold still prevents favorable numerical ranking.

sections.title: Growth Quality and Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: The bottom-up model separates FY26 goods ₹28.9263 crore, services/design ₹48.53075 crore after Media allocation, and Media ₹2.82475 crore. The split is a modeling proxy, not segment disclosure. Media uses 200 deployment units as management-claim proxy, with implied starting annual revenue per unit ₹1.412 lakh; actual revenue-producing unit count, ownership timing, advertising fill and ARPU are not audited. Base assumptions grow services 15%, goods 25%, fleet 30% and per-unit monetization 5%, with 20% EBIT margin. These are deliberately not management pipeline conversion. FY27 capital spend ₹35 crore remains large despite falling from FY26 ₹64.1467 crore including advances; thereafter 15% of revenue funds retained hardware and capitalized development. JV support, operating working capital 52% of revenue and cash reserves are explicit. Even this case breaches modeled cash requirements without additional finance. No CAP credit is awarded from high reported ROCE: normalized EBIT falls as net fixed/software assets rise from ₹14.9954 to ₹67.8828 crore, while connected loans and NCI complicate attribution. Software amortization, replacement fleets, field service and customer acquisition are real costs. A market runway exists; accessible profitable reinvestment at attributable high returns is not yet demonstrated.

sections.title: Management, Governance and Execution
sections.text: The record contains both disclosure discipline and important reconciliation needs. March 2025 Vira drone plans were terminated 11 August 2026; the company says strategic/execution differences, no entity incorporation and no shares issued. This is evidence against counting promised drone activity as achieved, and prompt termination disclosure is counterevidence to concealment. June 2026 Medigo agreement creates a structure but supplies no disclosed commercial floor. October LuLu deployment is a live-network management claim, not an audited profit milestone. Equity has expanded materially, including FY25 bonus, FY26 warrant conversion/fresh issue, August and October 2026 conversions. Related Falcon loan ₹24.031 crore, World EMS ₹37.5 crore CCPS, SpaceBox deposit and subsidiary outside investment require arm's-length and recovery evidence. Promoter loan approval up to ₹100 crore on 30 September permits funding but does not establish execution. The July proposed ₹40 crore limit is not the latest ceiling. Subsidiary equity proceeds belong to the recipient group perimeter and cannot be double-added to parent cash. Voting material indicates approved resolutions; disclosed interested votes and invalid-vote presentation need careful reading, not an accusation of approval manipulation. GOV 5 preserves unmodified IFC and absence of proven misconduct while requiring minority-attributable capital reconciliation.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: Six fiscal years are retained with original scope, units and conflicting vintages. FY23 prospectus-restated PAT ₹3.1809 crore differs from AR 24 comparative ₹2.9187 crore; CFO and cash differ too. Neither is silently overwritten. FY25 original CFO−₹7.5466 crore becomes ₹9.8313 crore in FY26 comparative principally through ₹17.3778 crore long-term advances reclassification. Total cash changes reconcile, while the original financing component sum differs from its printed total by ₹6.4033 crore. May 2026 revision describes grouping errors with no PAT/EPS/net-worth/cash effect; later AR cash-flow presentation differs slightly again, conserving cash within ₹0.0001 crore rounding. That response is preserved, not extended to unrelated issues. Latest two-year CFO ₹21.4168 crore/PAT ₹34.3848 crore=0.623. FY26 FCF is−₹44.0004 crore before ₹8.5608 crore paid capex advances and−₹52.5612 crore after. Other income ₹6.7252 crore includes FX ₹5.8435 crore. Operating EBIT is PBT+finance+JVloss−otherincome=₹21.1076 crore. NOPAT at assumed 25% tax ₹15.8307 crore is not certified parent profit. Unmodified main and IFC reports coexist with audit-trail preservation wording contradictions, working-capital bank-return clause lacking reconciliation conclusion and no-term-loan wording despite SMFG LAP. CARO loan figures and detailed notes differ tenfold. The consolidated related-party table labels amounts as rupees although its magnitudes appear differently scaled; no unverified crore conversion is used. Foreign subsidiary reporting is described both management-certified unaudited and audited by others. Simple NCI net-asset share ₹2.13551 crore versus reported ₹0.0307 crore needs timing/rights/elimination explanation; it is not proof of misstatement. AOC 1 Media net assets differ by ₹230 between two rounded constructions, immaterial. Reported diluted EPS is preserved separately from issued shares: older values reflect restatement/bonus history and cannot be divided by current shares as if comparable. FY26 printed diluted denominator 14,447,360 differs from 14,293,460 issued at March-end; the weighted-average/potential-share bridge remains open, rather than alleging a proven EPS error. Latest current issued shares 14,556,560 and potential 14,970,360 after outstanding warrants are used only for current/forward capitalization. Current net-cash optics cannot replace the full obligations bridge.

sections.title: Valuation and Market Expectations
sections.text: The official quote and 14,556,560 current issued shares imply ₹2,265.2191 crore equity value. Reported group PAT P/E135.14 x, sales 28.22 x and conservative historical-cash operating EV/EBITDA 94.36 x are diagnostic, not validated parent-normalized valuation multiples. The stock price cannot make BQS worse; it matters for IAS. The intrinsic analysis is a dated annual cash-and-exit-enterprise model through 20 October 2031, using 12/15/18% hurdle sensitivities, explicit operating reinvestment, debt, working capital, cash floor, NCI economic haircut and non-operating asset recovery. No separate property/fleet/IP value is added to the operating EV. Current funding cannot be verified and all unrescued cases breach cash floors, so ordinary and non-rescue conditional IRRs/entry prices remain null. Separate rescue simulations issue shares at 70% of reference price with 2% fees and full dated dilution; these are counterfactual financing assumptions, not offers. Even bull rescue does not meet 15%. Base assumes 18 x terminal EBITDA versus headline current 94 x, so no rerating dependence. Reverse expectations searches 0–100% annual growth and requires funded bracketed crossing; no endpoint is relabeled a solution. DCF is deliberately omitted because another precision-heavy terminal calculation would not cure funding or attribution uncertainty. Two-way growth/multiple, collections, capex, tax, cash availability, NCI and optional warrant scenarios are embedded.

sections.title: Bear Case and Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: The strongest counterargument is that attractive robots and growing venue presence still need intensive capital, working capital and customer adoption before producing distributable cash. A slowdown in goods orders, low media fill, delayed hospital licensing or failure to collect unbilled services could coincide with fleet replacement and new development spending. Connected loans and CCPS may not be recoverable when needed. The bear cash model uses 2% services growth,5% goods growth,10% fleet growth without ARPU improvement,10% EBIT margin,70% working-capital intensity and 10 x exit EBITDA; no recovery of non-operating investments. Its cash-floor breach is hypothetical, not an observed payment default. Rescue at a 30% discount transfers more ownership to new capital and cannot protect prior holders from business-value loss. The thesis-break variable is collected parent-attributable cash return on the installed/development base, not robot announcements. Counterevidence is meaningful: reported cash, recent paid warrant exercises, unmodified opinions, legitimate goods/services growth and actual deployment claims could support successful scaling. Those positives keep the judgment unresolved rather than fraud/failure, but cannot establish a margin of safety at today's reference valuation.

sections.title: 5× and10× Feasibility
sections.text: Fivefold equity value would require roughly ₹11,326 crore and tenfold ₹22,652 crore before additional dilution. At 18 x exit EBITDA and 24% EBITDA margin, the optimistic no-claims scale hurdles are approximately ₹2,622 crore and ₹5,244 crore revenue, respectively, from ₹80.28 crore FY26. These simple hurdles deliberately omit future financing dilution, minority economics, cash deficits and taxes on disposals; the actual parent-holder requirement is higher. The detailed formula table gives required five-year revenue CAGR rather than assuming product pipeline equals revenue. A large global TAM is insufficient: Kody would need manufacturing/service capacity, funded retained fleets, monetized advertising utilization, collections and defensible unit margins simultaneously. No probability is assigned to 5×/10×. Classification is unsupported on audited attributable evidence, not mathematically impossible. Reopen only after comparable recurring revenue and incremental returns become measurable; do not infer a multibagger just from small revenue scale.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Monitor eight decision-linked items. First, published H 1 FY 27 results: billed versus unbilled, group/standalone and cash collections; require a complete ₹10.5406 crore opening unbilled bridge, not a percentage-growth headline. Second, receivables aged 6–12 months:₹27.9421 crore baseline; migration beyond one year without payment is a warning. Third, full bank-return/audit-trail/term-loan and NCI reconciliations; unresolved repeat contradictions preserve G2 Hold. Fourth, operating cash and capex: FY26 ₹11.5855 crore versus ₹64.1467 crore including advances; funding must cover remaining commitments and downside cash floor. Fifth, Medigo actual license status, paid units, minimum contract value and collections; no medical approval assumed today. Sixth, Media/LuLu revenue-producing units, ARPU, venue share, maintenance cost and renewal cohorts; distinguish live units from cumulative pilots. Seventh, Falcon loan recoveries, World EMS conversion/exit rights and subsidiary outside-equity allocation. Eighth, current shares, optional warrant exercise receipts, promoter-loan drawdowns and restrictions. Reassess after results or material financing disclosure; no automatic trading trigger. A cheaper price alone cannot cure reliability/funding gates.

sections.title: Final Classification and Conditional Action
sections.text: Hold — unresolved; pending evidence rather than a ranked low-quality or cheap investment. The business is an emerging software/robotics transition with optionality, not a proven high-return compounder. All three aggregates are NS and ineligible for numerical ranking; G2 financial reliability and G3 funding/survival remain Hold. G1 minority protection and G4 tradability are Conditional rather than failed. Current valuation is demanding even under the separate explicitly financed upside case, but a numerical IAS return factor cannot be justified while attributable financeable economics remain unknown. No ordinary target, entry price or position recommendation is provided. The next useful action is to obtain publicly disclosed reconciliation of audited annexures, capital/NCI and collected contract economics, then verify a conservative current resources/uses bridge and rebuild parent-holder returns. Evidence sufficient for gate improvement need not include private daily bank statements. Until then, paper sensitivity values are not executable offers and do not establish an acceptable probability of permanent loss.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions and Open Questions
sections.text: The source register links exact original primary filings and preserves SHA 256 digests. Full originals, extracted text and three inspected material page images remain local research evidence; portable analytical backups intentionally contain financial extracts and source metadata only. Reproduction verifies arithmetic and internal consistency, not fresh authenticity of issuer statements. Official NSE bhavcopies and master authenticate quote/lot/series; issuance filings override stale master equity counts. Peer annual reports are economic context, not current market comparable valuations. Information after 20 October 2026 is excluded. Every forward growth, margin, fleet proxy, capital intensity, collection schedule, asset recovery, NCI haircut and rescue issue price is an analyst assumption and separately stress-tested. Open questions are exact FY23 restatement bridge, CFO classification residuals, bank/annexure contradictions, revenue acceptance and collectability, parent equity/NCI rights, development amortization, unrestricted current cash, capital creditors, promoter-loan drawdown and warrant conversion, medical licenses, patent claims, robot unit cash returns and contract minima. Ordinary investment returns remain null until material feasibility gaps close. Analysis is general research, not individualized advice or a trade instruction.

FY25_cashflow_bridge.principal_reclassification: ₹17.3778cr long-term advances included in original CFO; moved to investing substantially explains CFO change. Interest and other classification changes offset remaining CFI/CFF shifts. This is not ₹17.38cr of new collections.

revenue_mix.qualification: Goods/services note is not a robot model/recurring software split. FY26 unbilled export exceeds total year-on-year revenue addition; services include robotics/design and related-party sales. Group subsidiaries are greenfield, not evidence of bought third-party revenue; organic monetization bridge nevertheless incomplete.

working_capital_FY26.proxy_definition: Trade receivables + unbilled + inventory + trade advances + assumed other operating assets1.0 − trade payables − other account payables − customer advances. Last two classifications and realization need reconciliation. Tax balances excluded.

claims_FY26.unverified_lease_obligation: ND; AS operating rent included in operating costs, not assumed zero lease commitments.

perimeter.NCI_gap_not_proven_error: Simple proportion ignores acquisition dates, consolidation eliminations and rights. ₹2.1048cr difference needs ownership/premium/elimination worksheet. Do not call ordinary standalone-versus-consolidated differences errors.

capitalization.reason: No attributable deployed-fleet, software/IP cohort margin, full reinvestment or mature return series; shifting perimeter and capitalization mean aggregate ROCE is not incremental return proof.

share_bridge.forfeiture_status_of_old_4000_warrants: FY26 note old application zero; no additional old warrants assumed. This needs confirmation rather than adding proceeds.

growth_analysis.REV_scoring_basis: Above30% threshold robust to billed-services-only diagnostic; not a precise organic estimate; Medium-confidence ceiling8

valuation.units: INR crore unless price, shares, dates or percentages stated
valuation.day_basis: Actual days for fiscal allocations; exactly five calendar anniversaries for equity return.

valuation_crosschecks.PE: Market/reported consolidated PAT is diagnostic only because FY26 parent attribution and sustainable earnings remain unresolved. No fair PE-derived price.
valuation_crosschecks.DCF: Not used. Funding, reinvestment and parent cash attribution are too uncertain for a separately precise DCF; annual cash model and exit-EV crosschecks expose these dependencies.
valuation_crosschecks.asset_value: World EMS CCPS and Falcon/Platinum loans enter terminal recovery at 0/50/100% of reported cost only; not current funding. Operating property/fleet/software not separately added. Existing warrant deposit already in cash/equity and never added as new cash.

valuation.scenario_assumptions_basis: All growth, margins, fleet proxy, capital intensity, NCI economic haircut, asset recovery and exit multiples are analyst assumptions, not guidance or commitments. Services includes design and unbilled work, not pure recurring software; media fleet200 proxy is management claim, not audited deployed/revenue-producing units. FY27 capital spend25/35/50 cr is explicit slowdown from FY26 64.1467 cr cash including advances; stress+50%.

limits: Opening cash31.6223 excludes11.2314 debit OD and.0016 warrant account; no claim these are proven restricted. All FD3.4134 excluded including explicitly liened3.0. Known warrant receipts19.2391875 included only at actual Aug7 and Oct12 dates. Optional30.259125 not assumed in base.

Existing tax provision8.1273 plus2.2521 other current provisions/duties/MSME interest/employee payable settled once Sep30 assumption, not added to future tax rate expense. Current debt maturity included in opening debt, not added twice. Gratuity/leave cash0.03/year assumption; residual1.0908 less modeled settlements and rent deposit0.135 deducted terminally.

Working capital proxy includes20.5315 other account payables as operating. If capital creditors, reclassify both opening NWC and settlement together, not add standalone20.5315 again. Model uses accrual capex-to-cash assumptions; creditor uncertainty is material to G3.
No bank headroom, uncommitted promoter loan, receivable collection, FD release or World EMS sale is established current funding. Loan ceiling approval up to100cr is not drawdown.

NCI economic haircut3/5/10% of operating EV and positive surplus only; full cash deficits remain parent claims is a scenario proxy, not reported NCI. Full debt remains deducted; parent distributions, subsidiary restrictions and consolidated equity allocation need reconciliation.
FY32 is used only to interpolate the terminal date; no post-20 October 2031 cash flow or gap affects investor outputs. Monthly/end-event tests cannot prove intramonth solvency.
